newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds rally following bank rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds rally following bank rate cut.

text.p: Canadian bonds were stronger in heavy trading on Wednesday, outperforming their U.S. counterparts following a rate cut by the Bank of Canada, traders said.

"Bonds themselves are rallying but having difficulty at this level. I think we've reached a technical resistance point on the Canadian long bonds," said Hank Cunningham, a bond trader with First Marathon Securities.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.53 at C$104.65 to yield 7.590 percent against the U.S. 30-year benchmark which gained 9/32 to yield 6.85 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 74 basis points from 76 basis points at Tuesday's close.
The Bank of Canada this morning cut short-term interest rates for the eighth time this year, lowering its key bank rate by 25 basis points to 4.0 percent.

It was the seventh time this year the bank has cut rates independent of an easing by the U.S. Federal Reserve. The bank has now lowered short-term rates by 200 basis points this year and 425 basis points since May 1995.
The Bank's target range for its overnight lending rate is now 3.50-4.0 percent, down from 3.75-4.25 percent.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.39 to C$99.95 to yield 7.005 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 6/32 to yield 6.62 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds narrowed to 39 basis points from 43 basis points at Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.61 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.05 percent.
